approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves scored molecular graphs with crossover and mutation, draws breeding parents from high-scoring bands of its current survivor population, and keeps a full archive of accepted scores. Before each new proposal batch, a Gaussian process fits every accepted record using local molecular count fingerprints. It evaluates a fresh pool of offspring through correlated sampled functions and selects their available maxima. Real offspring scores update both this predictor and the score-greedy breeding population. Direct aromatic carbon/nitrogen exchange is disabled, while continuation, crossover finishing mutation, stable identity admission and bounded numerical fallbacks remain active.
approach.novelty: Control the ongoing-learning path by fitting the same active Gaussian process only to immutable copies of the original usable initial observations at every suggestion. Its initial training membership, labels and normalization stay fixed together. Later accepted scores still enter the full archive and determine live survivors and breeding parents. This differs from removing predictive selection or fixing breeding parents: current offspring still receive correlated GP predictions and evaluation choices, but generated labels cannot teach that predictor. The experiment asks what this one feedback path contributes, rather than proposing that a static predictor is a better optimizer.

observed_bottleneck: The current evidence does not separate useful initial GP guidance from useful ongoing conditioning on generated accepted labels. In n-62daf219c70a all 435 fits reconstruct from the actual earlier accepted archive in insertion order, growing from ten records at batch one to 290 at batch 29. Across the fifteen sessions, 4,200 distinct generated accepted records enter a later fit, with 60,900 repeated generated training rows; 150 terminal accepted records have no next fit. Every one of 420 post-initial fits changes both empirical mean and scale from its initial values, and all 4,200 accepted previous-emission probes change mean and uncertainty. All 435 current pools have nonzero cross-candidate covariance, and 3,755 of 4,350 sampled choices differ from the masked posterior-mean choice. These are observed updating and selection exposure, not the conditional contribution of updating. The full-pool composite-selector control n-01b48dd09404 loses paired mean 0.12438789088524467 while keeping model computation passive, whereas the frozen-initial-breeder control n-4d4b5eafa8b3 loses 0.260205546950089 while retaining all generated-label GP learning. Neither supplies the initial-only predictive control. Incumbent allocation n-8a62df15e51f, added atom-pair covariance n-e75f0f495f9b and rank targets n-ae12ccae8c7b all activate and miss their score goals, with distinct task/seed counterexamples; better selected-stream metrics or internal utility therefore cannot settle this narrower learning question. The limiting knowledge gap is the total value of continued generated-label conditioning within the already useful active selector.
hypothesis: Freeze the active count-Tanimoto GP training dataset to immutable copies of the original usable initial accepted archive in its original order for every inherited fit, jointly freezing its empirical label normalization while retaining full real-archive feedback for live graph breeding and the original correlated posterior allocation on fresh pools.

finding_summary.headline: Continued GP conditioning contributes: initial-only training lowers every matched endpoint and the mean by 0.151856.
finding_summary.insights:
Ongoing conditioning on generated accepted observations adds value beyond an initially fitted predictor in this optimizer, even when real-label survival, recursive breeding and posterior selection remain active. The experiment therefore answers a narrower question than removing the whole selector or freezing the breeding cohort. Training membership, later label information and empirical normalization were held together: their individual effects, and their interaction with survival, remain unassigned. All sitagliptin fits retain the initial scale floor, but this exposure alone does not establish that the floor causes its endpoint losses.

Useful local search persists under the frozen predictor. It produces 580 best-parent wins and 125 incumbent advances, and every endpoint exceeds its initial best. The molecular assessment finds recognizable amide and aromatic-carbonyl families, useful available amines, changed linkers and ring closures. Some lower-scoring Child leaders have more conventional local chemistry than their Parent counterparts; other outputs retain reactive bonds, doubtful ring geometry and unresolved stereochemistry. The loss does not establish absent chemical novelty, require reactive motifs or identify a chemical mediator. Three leaders arrive in the final batch and cannot show later feedback effects.

The lower selected-stream prediction error is measured on different molecules and cannot establish better calibration or replace the endpoint contrast. Likewise, passive full-archive calculations change all 420 later selected sets on the actual Child pools, but do not supply alternative rewards or future histories. This complete exposed result ends the registered initial-cohort control. Shared-Parent sibling experiments and historical repeated trajectories are dependent evidence, so their effects cannot be added or treated as independent replications.
finding_summary.results:
All 435 GP fits keep the same ten initial accepted molecules, raw labels and normalization within each task/seed. Across 420 later fits, 4,200 generated observations remain in the real archive but never enter training; the 150 final observations have no later fit opportunity. Predictions for the same previously emitted molecule stay fixed to numerical precision. The selector remains active on every fresh 160-member pool, with nonzero correlated draws. Recursive breeding also remains active: 1,751 accepted offspring later serve as parents in 102,673 draws.

Every first batch matches the Parent. In batch two, the same pool and normal draws produce different evaluated sets after the first excluded feedback; parent and pool histories diverge in batch three. All three replicas complete. Mean final Top-1 falls from 0.595670 to 0.443813, a paired change of -0.151856 against the predicted loss scale of 0.002. Seed changes are -0.181637, -0.118363 and -0.155569. All fifteen endpoints and all five task means decline. The zaleplon result in seed zero nearly matches its Parent, losing only 0.000484, while the largest loss is 0.430456 in docking seed two. Seed dispersion also falls, around the lower mean.

molecular.headline: Familiar aromatic amides and carbonyl heterocycles persist, with useful amines but incomplete context control and reactive ring chemistry
molecular.overall_character: All supplied Child n-7de8feaf821f and published Parent n-62daf219c70a trajectories were present and read. The brief independently reports child_complete=true and paired_complete=true for Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2, with no profile mismatch or uncovered objective. Each task contributes 900 Child records, including 870 optimizer evaluations; all matched task/seed initial molecule and score records agree. Every Child retained best exceeds its fixed initial best, while all fifteen matched Parent endpoints remain higher. The seed-0 indole-amide comparison is nearly matched, whereas several available-amine and fluorinated-heterocycle comparisons differ substantially. The Child produces recurrent indole carboxamides, aryl-linked nitrogen/carbonyl systems, amide and sulfonamide material with available amines, and bridged or fused nitrogen rings. Many recognizable initial functional-group arrangements remain visible in leading output, but actual recursive breeding also produces changed linkers, new ring closures and useful simplifications. There is moderate chemical diversity across families and seeds, with narrower useful leading neighborhoods; this is not global structural collapse or an inability to produce rings. In fixed task order the digest ring-closure-string incidences are 0.9931, 0.9471, 0.969, 0.9828 and 0.954, and aromatic-string incidences are 0.9931, 0.9425, 0.9575, 0.9586 and 0.9241. These are text-feature incidences, not perceived ring counts or aromatic-atom fractions. Formal-charge and stereocentre-string incidences are 0.0 throughout. The respective cross-seed distinct-identity counts are 841, 870, 876, 874 and 870; each task/seed still has 300 distinct accepted identities. Cross-seed recurrence is not within-run duplicate evaluation. The moderate drug-likeness reading reflects familiar amides, ethers, carbonyl heterocycles and available amines in many leaders. It does not imply confirmed activity or easy synthesis. Synthetic plausibility remains questionable because other accepted molecules carry N-F or O-Cl bonds, peroxide/peracid groups, unusual imines and four-membered or bridged closures, and because very large joined products recur. Several conventional Child indole-amide and amine leaders avoid reactive bonds found in their Parent counterparts, so lower observed scores do not uniformly mean worse chemical plausibility. Read-only RDKit descriptors were calculated from the supplied trajectories; no objective, affinity or synthesis score was generated. The authorized source and receipts distinguish the immutable original usable accepted GP cohort from the complete real observation archive and the live score-ranked breeding population. Across the recorded Child fits, the initial ten training records and their label mean/scale remain the training basis, while final real archives contain all 300 accepted records. The later accepted leaders have genuine raw scores, enter the real archive and survive by the inherited score law; their absence from GP training is not rejection or loss of genetic feedback. For example, the seed-0 amine/amide leader appears in the next context as a live rank-0 survivor and archived observation but not a training member, and later actually breeds a high-scoring accepted analogue. The same distinction holds for a leading pyridyl indole amide whose later accepted descendant loses useful context and scores poorly. These are molecular provenance examples, not an activation verdict. The full-pool receipts retain the inherited pool size, and current molecules still receive current predictions and correlated selection draws. A fixed training cohort does not mean constant predictions for different molecules, frozen pools, static initial breeders or removal of the selector. The inherited archive_mean prediction field is explicitly scoped in these receipts to the initial training mean; its name does not make it the current complete-archive mean. Training membership, later-label information and empirical normalization are held together in this control; their separate effects, whole-selector contribution and whole-foundation contribution are not identified here. All thirty Child/Parent task/seed leaders were joined to actual pooled, emitted and accepted records and their generating scored parents. Initial-source molecules, unscored graph intermediates, pooled offspring, emitted proposals, accepted observations, live survivors, actual breeders and retained-best endpoints remain distinct. Some late leaders have no later feedback opportunity; another recorded leader breeds a chlorinated pooled analogue with no accepted label. No score or chemical benefit is imputed to that unqueried molecule. Chemical frequencies and missing-feature statements concern accepted trajectories and leaders, not a census of the full unselected pool. The digest final_molecules are late seed-2 observations, not all seeds' retained best. The original gap reports in n-c55c3d520a2c and their identical-trajectory carry-forward in n-62daf219c70a were read through the fresh legal evidence index. Historical reproduction is provenance, not independent replication. This single complete matched panel shares a Parent baseline with other current routes and has adaptive histories; no independent-replication, combined, additive or interaction claim follows. Chemical association and overlapping ancestry do not establish mediation or separate predictive from survival contributions. All supplied source, trajectory and log paths were present. Audits under .slots/r0020-03-ablation-L01/molecular/ preserve trajectory descriptors, source/log hashes, leader_training_provenance.json, original gap provenance and citation joins. Only Child digest/trusted-trajectory SMILES are quoted; Parent-only molecules are identified by their published task, seed and evaluation.

per_task.generated_character: Accepted offspring have median 25 heavy atoms and three perceived rings, with the leading structures retaining an NH-indole carboxamide linked to a fluoroaniline or pyridyl ring. The seed-0 leader at evaluation 272 has 24 heavy atoms, methoxy/methyl substitution and a mercaptomethyl group; seed 1/evaluation 101 has 24 heavy atoms and a vinyl ether, methoxy and pyridyl amide; seed 2/evaluation 145 has 23 heavy atoms with methoxy and two methyl groups. All three are recognizable compact aromatic amides without N-halogen bonds or carbon cumulenes. The vinyl ether and free thiol still pose local stability questions, but these leaders are more conventional than many Parent leaders. The Parent endpoints at seed 0/evaluation 289, seed 1/evaluation 293 and seed 2/evaluation 294 instead include an N-chloroindole cumulene, an N-fluoro/N-hydroxy pyridyl amide and an N-chloroindole aryl diketone. The complete Child stream also contains doubled indole assemblies, reactive halogen/peroxide derivatives and fragments; its conventional leaders do not describe every evaluated molecule.
liabilities: Vinyl ether and free-thiol substitution in two leaders requires stability scrutiny; other accepted derivatives introduce N-halogen, O-halogen or peroxide connections.
Joined bis-indole products reach 49 heavy atoms and extremely low observed scores, while small late derivatives can lose the beneficial pendant aromatic/amide context.
missing_features: The useful compact aromatic-amide organization is present, but the evaluated leading family offers few comparably useful alternatives beyond peripheral substituent changes; the stronger Parent polar-group arrangements are not consistently reached.

There is no demonstrated need for the Parent leaders' N-halogen or cumulene motifs: a conventional Child amide nearly matches one Parent endpoint, while other families remain below their matched endpoints.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial trimethoxyindole fluoroanilide scores 0.3051048083696145. The three Child leaders improve that value while retaining the connected fused-aromatic/amide/polar arrangement. Seed-1 evaluation 101 at 0.40282869817021466 is the logged deletion product of a fluoropyridyl relative at evaluation 46 (0.36941374410829103). That leader remains live and later breeds despite being absent from GP training. Its first recorded later emitted descendant, the much smaller C=N-O-N-aryl product at evaluation 111, scores 1.9668318815584645e-09. The doubled indole at seed 0/evaluation 126 scores 4.676896037450175e-19, while the late seed-2 N-fluoroamide with lost pendant aryl context at evaluation 295 scores 0.0023822240071644405. Thus neither extensive joining nor aggressive fragmentation preserves the favorable context. The seed-0 mercaptomethyl leader at 0.393567030299894 nearly matches its Parent endpoint 0.39405142067435733, while the other two Child endpoints are further below their Parent values. This is a useful favorable local-chemistry counterexample to a uniform deterioration narrative, without demonstrating a missing required reactive group. Complete matched retained-best scores, Child / Parent, are seed 0: 0.393567030299894 / 0.39405142067435733; seed 1: 0.40282869817021466 / 0.47411701813450596; seed 2: 0.38277504802042894 / 0.438972502037081. These observed endpoints do not identify a chemical mediator.

per_task.generated_character: Accepted offspring have median 30 heavy atoms and four rings, spanning compact nitrogen-rich heterocycles, linked unsaturated aromatic systems and very large joined products. The 25-heavy-atom seed-0 leader at evaluation 289 links a hydroxy nitrogen-dione region to an unusual aza-fused system containing a four-membered imine closure. The 41-heavy-atom seed-1 leader at evaluation 290 has extended fused aromatic/azaaryl character, an ethynyl group, a conjugated imine/alkene linker, an ethoxy substituent and an ethyl peroxide. The 27-heavy-atom seed-2 leader at evaluation 289 combines an N-fluorinated fused heteroaromatic/ether framework with a fluorinated amino-methine, diazine and formate ester. The Parent seed-0 leader at evaluation 281 has a different cross-linked carbonyl/thione architecture with O-F and a halomethyl ether; seeds 1/evaluation 296 and 2/evaluation 296 retain linked azaaryl/cyanate and peroxide-bearing arylamine chemistry. Neither panel supplies uniformly conventional synthesis targets.
liabilities: Ethyl peroxide, an N-F aromatic nitrogen, fluorinated amino-methine and a small fused imine closure raise local stability, geometry or synthesis questions.
The accepted stream includes both near-floor fragments and exceptionally large joined molecules; multiple rings and valid graph syntax do not establish useful or feasible chemistry.
missing_features: The evaluated Child does not reliably reach the Parent leaders' useful heteroaromatic arrangements, especially the compact seed-0 cross-linked family; no single absent functional group is sufficient to explain the three seed gaps.

Stable, chemically credible alternatives to the peroxide, N-F and unusual small-ring environments remain incomplete among the leading structures; useful carbonyl and aromatic connectivity is already present.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The small altered aza-ring at seed 0/evaluation 152 scores 0.5030188028290494, a partially saturated carbonyl heterocycle at seed 1/evaluation 47 scores 0.5130890052356021, and the small imine/cyclopentadiene at seed 2/evaluation 57 scores 0.5008688852202624. The initial best is 0.548381482770623; all Child leaders exceed it. The seed-2 leader is a logged ring-closure product of evaluation 210 (0.5885769857540872), reaching 0.6013780125053118. The seed-1 leader at 0.6036096256684492 comes from crossover plus atom replacement involving the conjugated peroxide-bearing evaluation 206 (0.6015096304008329) and a larger multiaryl parent. A still larger 115-heavy-atom joined product at seed 1/evaluation 296 scores 0.5851570574753966, below that leader; methyl fluoride at seed 0/evaluation 294 remains at the 0.5 floor. The visible gradient favors some extended heteroaromatic/polar arrangements over fragments, but not arbitrary growth. The seed-1 leader later generates a chlorinated pool member that has no accepted trajectory record; no value is assigned to that unqueried alternative. All Child endpoints are lower than the matched Parent endpoints, with the seed-0 Parent-specific architecture accounting for the largest local gap; this does not prescribe its reactive O-F bond as a missing requirement. Complete matched retained-best scores, Child / Parent, are seed 0: 0.5925633411259241 / 0.8561477222467935; seed 1: 0.6036096256684492 / 0.6248206599713055; seed 2: 0.6013780125053118 / 0.6178024026512013. These observed endpoints do not identify a chemical mediator.

per_task.generated_character: Accepted offspring have median 40 heavy atoms and molecular weight about 624.4, compared with Parent medians of 31 heavy atoms and about 476.7; both have median four rings. Much Child output retains bulky aryl/amide/sulfonamide context, although useful available amines do emerge. The 29-heavy-atom seed-0 leader at evaluation 265 contains N-propyl pyrrolidine, a carboxamide, dichlorophenyl substitution and an eight-membered unsaturated N/O ring. The 33-heavy-atom seed-1 leader at evaluation 206 is an indene-like aryl thiol with methoxy/fluoro substitution, amide and a flexible secondary-amine chain ending in aryl sulfonamide. The 39-heavy-atom seed-2 leader at evaluation 258 has an N-substituted pyrrolidine amide, fused oxygen ring/biaryl material, a dichlorodienyl chain, hydroxymethyl and an O-Cl substituent. Parent leaders at seed 0/evaluation 284, seed 1/evaluation 261 and seed 2/evaluation 241 contain differently arranged diaryl tertiary or cyclic amines, generally without the same retained amide/sulfonamide load. The Child seed-0 and seed-1 leaders avoid heteroatom-halogen bonds; the seed-2 leader does not.
liabilities: The O-Cl bond, thiol and unsaturated or enlarged ring contexts require stability or synthesis scrutiny; the seed-0 and seed-1 leaders provide counterexamples without reactive heteroatom-halogen bonds.
High typical size and unspecified saturated-centre stereochemistry weaken a strong drug-likeness interpretation despite recognizable amines, amides and aryl groups.
missing_features: Useful available-amine/aromatic organization is present but unevenly combined with the remaining polar and steric context; the Child does not reliably reach the Parent's compact successful arrangements.

Selective simplification is incomplete: many accepted molecules remain large amide/sulfonamide assemblies even though more compact useful amines occur. Neither absence of all amines nor a universal need to remove polar groups describes this output.
Explicit stereochemical identities are missing for substituted pyrrolidines, benzylic amides and fused saturated rings; this is an identity limitation, not a measured docking penalty.

per_task.generated_character: Accepted offspring have median 31 heavy atoms and four rings. Their familiar motifs are diaryl or quinoline regions connected to nitrogen/carbonyl rings, with frequent altered ring closures. The seed-0 leader at evaluation 285 has 32 heavy atoms, a substituted hydroxy/chloro azaaryl ring, fluorophenyl group and fused nitrogen/medium-ring lactam framework. The seed-1 leader at evaluation 289 has 30 heavy atoms and a quinoline connected to a densely bridged imine-containing nitrogen system with a four-membered unsaturated ring and a dicarbonyl region. The seed-2 leader at evaluation 293 has 30 heavy atoms: an ethoxy-substituted diaryl N/O ring linked by an exocyclic double bond to a seven-membered nitrogen-dicarbonyl ring, without a peroxide or N-O bond. Parent leaders retain related diaryl/quinoline and N/O-carbonyl combinations, including a seed-0 N-O bridge and different medium-ring connections at seeds 1 and 2. The Child has substantial ring chemistry, but its geometrical and functional-group organization is not consistently as useful under the observed scores.
liabilities: Four-membered unsaturation, dense bridges and N-N/C=N variants are not validated by exact score ties or successful SMILES parsing.
Potential saturated and bridge stereocentres are unspecified in some leaders; the flatter seed-2 leader has no detected tetrahedral stereocentre and limits any blanket claim.
missing_features: The generator does not consistently preserve the favorable combined aromatic/carbonyl-ring arrangement when it fragments, joins or closes graphs; the stronger matched Parent arrangements are not reached at these endpoints.

Chemically credible alternatives to the strained-looking four-membered/bridged nitrogen closure are incompletely represented among the leaders, although the peroxide-free seed-2 diaryl/dicarbonyl product is a concrete more conventional counterexample.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial best is 0.1678386594791329; all three Child leaders improve it. The seed-1 acidic anilide at evaluation 14 scores 0.07504633196017493, the seed-2 small bridged N/O-carbonyl thiol at evaluation 98 scores 0.07429784553659712, and the 72-heavy-atom seed-0 assembly at evaluation 44 scores 0.12171727980511543. The favorable examples need combined aromatic and carbonyl-ring context rather than just small polar fragments or enlarged repeats. A logged bond change from the seed-1 evaluation-244 precursor (0.1902459009410157) gives evaluation 289 at 0.1921478581921902; its actual later N-N/C=N analogue at evaluation 291 ties exactly at 0.1921478581921902. These equal scores do not make the changed heteroatom linkage chemically equivalent. The earlier leader breeds while remaining outside training. Seed-2 evaluation 293 at 0.20936936917042825 is an actual crossover product from evaluation 266 (0.19284667698451546) and a peroxide-bearing parent at evaluation 258 (0.18789047556952765). The product has no peroxide: useful molecular reorganization is possible with the retained recursive channel. Its terminal batch leaves no later training-probe or breeding opportunity. All Child endpoints remain below their matched Parent, and the supplied scores do not isolate a beneficial individual ring closure or heteroatom. Complete matched retained-best scores, Child / Parent, are seed 0: 0.18511217506480454 / 0.2258403994203931; seed 1: 0.1921478581921902 / 0.2214095461892601; seed 2: 0.20936936917042825 / 0.22600312875247064. These observed endpoints do not identify a chemical mediator.

per_task.generated_character: Accepted offspring have median 27 heavy atoms and four rings, repeatedly retaining nitrogen-dione, aryl and phenol-derived chemistry. The seed-0 leader at evaluation 174 has 28 heavy atoms: a fluorinated fused aza-aromatic/dione system with an N-acyl cyclopentadiene substituent, without N-halogen or carbon cumulene. The seed-1 leader at evaluation 293 has 26 heavy atoms, a phenyl-substituted fused N-fluoro dione and a fluorinated hydroxycyclopentenyl group with unspecified stereochemistry. The seed-2 leader at evaluation 294 has 27 heavy atoms, an N-methyl dione linked to phenol and an N-fluorinated, carbon-fluorinated pyrrole. Compared with the Parent seed-0 small unsaturated nitrogen-ring/imino family, seed-1 fluoroalkenyl dione and seed-2 cyclic-cumulene/nine-membered nitrogen-ring leader, the Child leaders remain closer to familiar aromatic-dione arrangements. Large joined dione assemblies can score far below their simpler relatives, while noncumulated leaders do not imply that the full accepted stream lacks cumulenes.
missing_features: The evaluated Child leaders do not reach the Parent's strongest compact fluorinated/imino arrangements, but the molecular evidence does not show that an N-F bond or cyclic cumulene is the missing causal requirement.

Stable alternatives that retain useful fluorinated context remain uneven: a non-N-halogen dione is already competitive within one Child seed, while other leaders still carry N-F bonds or unusual acyl/fused connectivity.
Stereochemical identity remains unspecified for the hydroxyfluorocyclopentenyl leader; its possible score consequences were not evaluated.

transferable_gaps.evidence: This gap originates in n-c55c3d520a2c and is retained through the identical published chemistry of n-62daf219c70a; historical reproduction is not independent replication. Current evidence is n-7de8feaf821f versus n-62daf219c70a on complete matched Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2, 300 observations per objective, batch size 10 and the frozen Research-in-Depth epoch-1 profile. The current control holds the original usable initial GP cohort, labels and empirical mean/scale together while keeping the complete real accepted archive, raw-label genetic survival/rank breeding, recursion and full correlated full-pool selector active. Evidence describes accepted chemistry and inspected provenance, not rewards or absence of chemistry in unselected pools, separate normalization effects or whole-selector/foundation contribution. Leading products retain indole carboxamides, aromatic nitrogen diones and amide/sulfonamide-rich aryl systems; within a seed, many useful changes are peripheral substitutions. Different seeds nevertheless reach distinct ring and linker families, useful deletions and available-amine products. Every Child retained best improves on its initial best. A conventional compact amide nearly matches one Parent endpoint, while the complete panel leaves other stronger Parent arrangements unreached. This is uneven useful coverage, not absent novelty or absent recursive generation.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently provide useful alternatives beyond recurring inherited functional-group and scaffold combinations in evaluated output.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Develop chemically coherent alternative arrangements under legal task-local feedback and assess their actual evaluated descendants, rather than treating identity counts or retained initial motifs as sufficient coverage. Real acceptance and genetic reuse must remain distinguishable from admission to a predictive training set. This molecular finding neither authorizes tuning the bounded training-cohort control nor isolates training membership, label information, normalization, survival or total optimizer effects.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
